caption:
Every photo in this post was taken on a phone. Not one of them was taken in a studio.

Here is the part nobody says out loud: your phone's camera has not been the weak link for years. A phone from 2019 already out-resolves anything Instagram will ever show you. The sensor is fine. The lens is fine.

What you never had was light.

A studio is not a room. It is a set of lights placed on purpose — one to shape the face, one to separate you from the background, one to open the shadows. That is the whole difference between a snapshot and a portrait, and it is the one thing a phone physically cannot add. There is no hot shoe. There is nowhere to mount a strobe. The shape of the phone decided that for you at the factory.

So we moved the lights to after the photo.

One picture, five setups. Slide 8 is a photo from 2022 shot on an iPhone 13, run through the same tool — because the point was never that you need a new phone. The point is that you never did.

💬 Every light has a number. Comment the number you want and I'll send that exact setup straight to you.

slides.title: Your phone was never the problem.

slides.title: A phone cannot hold a light.
slides.body: There is no hot shoe. Nowhere to mount a strobe, no trigger, no way to fire a light off camera. That is not a flaw in your phone — it is the shape of it, and it was decided for you at the factory. So we moved the lights to after the photo.
